title: GT1D-613SY - METHODOLOGY TO UPDATE OPERATIONAL MODELS OF A SPACECRAFT SYSTEM (EXPRO+)
description: Simulation models developed at design, AIT and operations phases shall be recalibrated based on the flight experience. Currently, during operation, the predictive simulations performed by design, AIT and operations teams with simulators are not fully connected toflight telemetry. Therefore, the simulators do not reflect the real state of the spacecraft and the lessons learned are not transferred to the models for the next spacecraft. The activity aims at streamlining the process, enhancing the fidelity and representativeness of the simulation models and reducing the effort for models update and reusability. In this activity, to implement the correction of the model, an assessment to define the origin of the deviation shall be made considering the latest advancement in digitalization, model calibration and synchronization, leveraging the concepts of digital twins' spacecraft. Furthermore, state of the art approaches of surrogate modelling, AI and Machine Learning shall be considered to enhance representativeness and fidelity. The experimentation plan shall be extended in a multidisciplinary way, to improve the method, including in-flight data, and to prepare multidisciplinary optimization to improve operations, future design and reduce the margins.

title: AI-AUGMENTED HAZARD DETECTION AND AVOIDANCE FOR THE L4 ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesAssess the feasibility of using physics-based granular dynamics simulation to model the formation of cryovolcanic terrains on Enceladus and derive insights into surface compactness. Develop a proof-of-concept ML model for inferring snow/ice geophysicalproperties (e.g., density, snow water equivalent) by correlating terrestrial in-situ scientific data with satellite remote sensing observations. Initiate the adaptation of classical, optimization-based HDA frameworks to integrate AIderived geophysical safety maps, establishing a baseline for a future hybrid HDA architecture. Conduct an extensive performance and resource consumption benchmark of key AI and HDA software components on representative space-grade hardware, establishing the trade-space between algorithmic capability and on-board computational budgetDescriptionThe ESA Voyage 2050 L4 mission to Enceladus requires an autonomous landing in the South Polar Terrain to achieve its core astrobiological objectives. This environment presents unique challenges that transcend classical HDA capabilities. Landing hazardsare not only geometric (e.g., slopes, rocks), but also geophysical. Due to the unknown load-bearing capacity of cryovolcanic surface deposits, landing sites can appear perfectly flat and clear of hazards and yet be catastrophically unsafe. Classical existing Hazard Detection and Avoidance (HDA) frameworks targeting Moon and Mars, are highly mature for geometric hazard assessment but are not designed to infer subsurface geophysical properties from remote sensing data. This activity shall address this critical technology gap by investigating the integration of AI/ML-based geophysicalinference into a proven HDA decision-making architecture. Additionally, the severe power and computational constraints of a solar-powered missionto Saturn imposea hard limit on the complexity of on-board AI. It is currently unknown what level of "intelligence" is achievable within a realistic resource budget. This activity shall perform the foundational trade-off analysis required to inform mission designers of the necessary hardware and power provisions for a reliable and capable AI-augmented HDA system

title: PHASED ARRAYS EXPLOITING GRATING LOBESFOR SCATTEROMETER INSTRUMENTS EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop a representative demonstrator of a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array with a reduced number of control points, by exploiting grating lobes.Description: For Earth Observation applications there are instruments, like Scatterometers, requiring a limited number of beams M pointing in fixed directions. A promising antenna architecture is based on an array antenna organized in interleaved subarrays (number of subarrays equal to the number of target beams M). Each subarray is having the periodic cell split in M sub-apertures. One of the M sub-apertures is occupied by a radiating element, the other M-1 slots are kept emptyto be used by the other M-1 interleaved subarrays. The dimension of the periodic cell is larger than one wavelength in order to create grating lobes exactly in the directions where the desired beams of the Scatterometer instrument are targeted. The array factor associated to the M phase centres of the M subarrays, when fed with identical phase value, creates a beam pointing at the boresight direction with radiative nulls positions coinciding with the grating lobes positions. Accordingly, when feeding the M inputs with thesame phase value a main beam in the boresight direction can be generated and the M-1 grating lobes can be cancelled by the radiative nulls. When feeding the M inputs with a linear phase in order to point the main beam exactly at one of the M possible targeted angles, the radiative nulls permit to cancel all the subarray pattern beams except the desired one. The M beams can be generated one atthe time, or simultaneously by adding a small beamforming MxM network. Possible values for M could be 3 or 5. To be noted also thatthecorresponding beams can be placed in the same azimuthal plane or not. This beamforming solution permits to reduce by a factor Mthe number of controls (phase shifters, direction couplers, amplifiers). As a consequence, a significant reduction in the cost and complexity of the entire instrument can be achieved. Reducing by a factor 3-5 the number of passive and active components in a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Instrument identification and requirements refinement. - Technology trade-off and down-selection. - Identification/optimization of most promising architectures. - Preliminary design of a baseline architecture and back-up architecture - Detailed design of a baseline architecture - Define preliminary manufacturing technique and prototype. - Definition of test and verification plan - Breadboard manufacturing and test - Results analysis and evaluation.

title: N2O SATELLITE OBSERVATION REQUIREMENTS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is an important greenhouse gas that also contributes to stratospheric ozone depletion. This study aims at characterising the needs for space-based observations of atmospheric N2O, starting from a user and science perspective. Knowledge gaps are identified related to the N2O production and life cycle, its impact on stratospheric ozone, and its role in the Earth's radiation balance that can be addressed with the help of satellite observations, with a focus on information that can be provided from satellite observations. The study explores the space of requirements that satellite observations of atmospheric N2O (Level-2) and measurements of radiances at the top of the atmosphere (Level-1) would have to meet in order to contribute to addressing these knowledge gaps.
